exposure: non-formation of bladder flap during Cesarean section
formation of bladder flap during Cesarean section
outcome: time to cut out the baby
number of gauze consumption during operation
cohort: The study included 64 pregnant women with a gestational age of 36 weeks or more who were undergoing their first Cesarean section.
finding: Omission of the bladder flap at Cesarean section resulted in short-term benefits, including reduced time to cut out the fetus, shorter duration of surgery, decreased intraoperative bleeding (less gauze consumption and hematocrit drop), and lower postoperative pain.
mod_finding: For women undergoing Cesarean section, omitting the bladder flap formation led to significant reductions in the time to cut out the baby, total operative time, intraoperative bleeding, and postoperative pain.
